languages_frameworks: React + Vite + TypeScript frontend (Cytoscape-style graph view)

implemented_capabilities.notes: Weighted-factor rule engine (execution->indicator path 0.40, malicious intel 0.25, ATT&CK 0.15, KEV vuln 0.15/0.10, privileged identity 0.10, critical asset reachability 0.10; clamp 0.05..0.95). Emits supporting_evidence_ids, missing_evidence and an uncertainty explanation. contradictory_evidence_ids is always an empty list (never populated).

Parameterised Cypher for Alert-[:HAS_EVENT]->Event-[:OCCURRED_ON]->Host-[:EXECUTED]->Process-[:CONNECTED_TO]->Indicator, Host-[:CAN_ACCESS]->Asset and Host-[:RUNS]->Software-[:AFFECTED_BY]->Vulnerability. The evidence subgraph query (MATCH p=(a)-[*1..4]-(t) ... LIMIT 40) explicitly filters out Investigation/ResponseAction/SimulatedState nodes to keep provenance apart from evidence topology.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Response policy and human approval gate state machine
implemented_capabilities.notes: States PROPOSED/WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL/APPROVED/EXECUTING/VERIFYING/VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED/DENIED/FAILED. execute_simulation raises PermissionError unless status==APPROVED; verification is action-specific. Actions only mutate an in-memory/JSON/FalkorDB 'simulated fleet', never real infrastructure. approver is accepted by approve_action/deny_action but not persisted on the record.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Provenance persistence of investigations and response actions
implemented_capabilities.notes: Investigation -INVESTIGATES-> Alert and Investigation -RECOMMENDED_ACTION-> ResponseAction written with timestamps (proposed/approved/executed/verified). State restored from FalkorDB or data/simulated_state.json on restart.

Template narrative with sections labelled Observed/Correlated/Hypothesis/Missing. get_llm_provider() returns DeterministicFallbackProvider even when an external LLM key and provider are configured (llm_provider.py:165-169), so no real LLM integration exists.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Custom scenario import with strict validation
implemented_capabilities.notes: Allowlist-checked labels and relationship types interpolated into Cypher, scalar-only property filtering, ID regex, entity/relationship caps, session scoping via session_id property.
Thin FastMCP wrappers around the same typed tools used by the orchestrator.
Fixed sequential pipeline: resolve alert -> run 5 graph queries -> assess -> narrative -> propose gated action -> persist. No LLM planning loop; AGENT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS in config is unused.

graph_models_and_cypher: Labels: Alert, Event, Host, Identity, Process, Indicator, Technique, Asset, Software, Vulnerability, Investigation, ResponseAction, SimulatedState, CustomScenario. Edges: HAS_EVENT, OCCURRED_ON, INVOLVES_IDENTITY, MAPS_TO, EXECUTED, CONNECTED_TO, CAN_ACCESS, RUNS, AFFECTED_BY, INVESTIGATES, RECOMMENDED_ACTION, DEFINES_ALERT. Indexes via 'CREATE INDEX FOR (x:L) ON (x.id)' (FalkorDB-native syntax). Uses fixed-shape multi-hop MATCH paths, OPTIONAL MATCH, any() over nodes(p), variable-length [*1..4] with LIMIT. No APOC/GDS. Session scoping through a session_id property rather than separate graphs.
algorithms: Weighted-factor deterministic risk score with bounded clamp (backend/scoring.py:assess_investigation)
Rule-based classification: LIKELY_COMPROMISE / SUSPICIOUS / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and priority matrix
Approval-gated action state machine with post-hoc verification (policy.py)
backend_interfaces: MCP stdio server backend/agent/mcp_server.py with 9 tools
frontend_interfaces: React/Vite components: AlertQueue, EvidenceGraph, FindingsPanel, ResponseActionPanel, NodeInspectorModal, RelationshipInspectorModal, ScenarioLabModal, Header
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: No LLM agent loop. Orchestrator is a deterministic pipeline. Persistent memory = Investigation and ResponseAction nodes in FalkorDB plus a simulated-fleet state store (FalkorDB SimulatedState nodes with JSON-file fallback). Human-in-the-loop approval gate with explicit status transitions; session isolation via session_id.
tests_present: 7 pytest files, ~59 test functions: test_api, test_custom_scenarios, test_graph_ablation (disposable graph proves topology changes classification), test_mcp_tools, test_policy_simulation (approval gate, restart persistence, session isolation), test_scoring, test_seed_validation. Most need a live FalkorDB.
security_findings: backend/api/routes.py:262-288 - approve/deny/execute endpoints have no authentication or authorization; approver identity is client-supplied and discarded (policy.py:400-410 never stores it)

backend/scenarios/service.py:126,149 - labels and relationship types interpolated into Cypher f-strings, but each is checked against server-side allowlists first (acceptable); property keys come from user JSON and are written via SET n += $props (property-key injection is not possible, but arbitrary property keys are written)
backend/policy.py:79 - MATCH (sm:SimulatedState) DELETE sm executed on reset (destructive, graph-wide for that label across sessions)
backend/policy.py:22-23,93 - writes data/simulated_state.json to local disk with no locking
backend/database.py:49 - failed queries are logged with full query text
backend/main.py:26-36 - CORS limited to localhost origins with allow_credentials=True (reasonable); no other findings
No subprocess/eval/exec/pickle; no hard-coded secrets (LLM_API_KEY read from env and unused).
duplicates_or_overlaps: Overlaps attack-path/alert-triage security investigation (ThreatNexus, exploit-path, other threat repos), vulnerability exposure (Host-Software-CVE), and approval-gated action workflows (decision lineage / change approval).
evidence_drift_relevance: MEDIUM - has a real approval-gate state machine with timestamped proposed/approved/executed/verified lifecycle, Investigation-to-ResponseAction provenance, and an explicit missing_evidence list, but no supersession, temporal validity or invalidation (contradictory_evidence_ids is never populated).

strongest_reusable_unit.why: Small, tested approval-gate lifecycle (propose -> require approval -> approve/deny -> execute only if approved -> verify) with durable persistence and restart survival, directly reusable as the approval-gating step in an Evidence Drift Cascade; scoring.py is a second portable unit for transparent factor-weighted scoring with missing-evidence reporting.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB optional (falls back to local JSON snapshot); no LLM key

strategy_rationale: A coherent, tested security-triage pack (alert context, attack path, KEV/asset exposure, deterministic scoring) that can be mounted as a Kairos capability pack, while the approval-gate class is worth extracting into a shared engine. Needs a license/attestation recorded before merging.
